issues: The original seventeenth-century text alleges marriage difficulty and marriage timing, but no birth certificates, verified marriages, nonmatches or prospective controls are given.
Earlier unnumbered seventh-house introduction addresses whether marriage occurs; this numbered CXXXI concerns obtaining marriage with ease and timing. They are different targets.
An earlier or later marriage and the age of the spouse at marriage are explicit alternative outcomes in the source, not interchangeable tests.
The source's age classes Youth, maturer years and very aged spouse have no specified cutoffs.
The east/Oriental and west/Occidental quarters use source-defined six-house lists that need historical astronomical geometry checks.
Moon Orientall of Sun versus general significators occidentall has different grammatical scope and prerequisites, not a simple house rule.
Direct/swift and retrograde/slow/stationary planetary states may contradict each other across multiple indicators, without deterministic weights.
When testimonies disagree, Lilly prioritizes indicator alignment with Moon then Venus, but provides no mathematical thresholds.
Lilly's personal anecdote of four adverse marriage placements does not report denominator, counterexamples, or observable full histories.
The source's sexual desire and lasciviousness claims are historically stigmatizing stereotypes, not facts about actual persons.
Sun/MC/Moon directions to Moon/Venus and seventh lord/benefic offer many overlapping potential event matches without selection policy.
Precise original direct/converse primary directions, Regiomontanus house geometry, aspect calculation, term/bounds table and arc-to-age conversion are NOT supplied.
Squares/oppositions to Sun/Mars are used with a Terms-of-a-Fortune caveat, not independently reproducible in this batch.
Qualitative marriage and partner-age claims, primary directions and source interpretation are preserved without runtime implementation.
Printed CXXXII on number of wives begins lower original PDF624 and belongs to a separate future source batch.
No woman/wife personal characterization, intimate behavior, birth date or future marriage prediction may be inferred from this source as established fact.
The packet is an anchored selective source paraphrase, not a complete diplomatic first-edition transcription.
